Bathurst Resources is New Zealand’s largest specialist coal producer with 4 local New Zealand coal mines. We produce over 2.2 million tonnes of coal each year and proudly employ over 550 people. About 80 percent of our production is used for steel making by local and international steel manufacturers. Our high-quality, thermal-grade coal fuels are also used to help drive the engines of many iconic New Zealand food and dairy businesses.

Our Stockton Mine is the largest opencast mine in New Zealand with a long history of high value coal production. It is located close to the coast on a plateau in the Buller coalfield, 35 km north of the Westport township, on the West Coast of the South Island. Think beaches, bush, mountains, rivers and lakes in our great outdoors, full of adventure potential!

Our organisation is culturally diverse and maintains a strong health and safety focus. We have our peoples’ best interests in mind and welcome you to put yourself forward to join our team if you have what it takes to do the job.

Near and in-pit field mapping.
In-pit guidance of production crews.

jobs.description:
Company Description
Luminia is a San Diego–based clean energy developer founded in 2019 that partners with not-for-profit clean electricity providers across California to deliver distributed solar and energy storage projects. The company focuses on strengthening grid resilience and creating long-term community benefits through a hyper-local approach that combines technical and financial expertise with strong community engagement and respect for local values. Luminia specializes in urban and commercial project siting to streamline permitting and interconnection, helping keep energy rates competitive while advancing clean energy goals. For commercial and industrial property owners, Luminia offers flexible financing and turnkey development solutions that unlock the value of rooftops and land, lower energy costs, and support sustainability objectives. With over 100 MW of distributed solar and storage in development, Luminia is committed to equitable, scalable projects that benefit the grid, the economy, and the communities it serves.

The Role

We're looking for a Project Coordinator to serve as the organizational backbone of our institutional partnership project pipeline. You'll track active projects from PPA execution through system energization, coordinating across internal engineering, external EPC partners, roofing contractors, tenants, and our institutional partner's team.

This isn't a role where you'll be making engineering or financial decisions. It's a role where you'll be the person who knows exactly where every project stands, who's responsible for the next step, and whether it's on track. When something slips, you'll be the first to notice and the first to flag it. When the engineering team is heads-down on technical work or pulled to another program, you'll be the voice keeping the institutional partnership projects moving.

Think of this as the connective tissue between our engineering team, our EPC partners, and our clients. The job is to make sure information flows, deadlines are tracked, and nothing gets deprioritized without a conscious decision.

What You'll Do

Project Tracking and Status Management

•        Maintain a comprehensive project tracker covering active projects from PPA execution through construction completion and permission to operate (PTO).
•       
Track key milestones: interconnection application submission and approval, permitting status, roof inspection and re-roof coordination, equipment procurement, construction scheduling, and PTO.
•       
Provide regular status updates to internal leadership and flag slippage or risks before they become problems.
•       
Ensure institutional partnership projects maintain priority and visibility when team resources are shared across programs.

Coordination and Communication

•        Coordinate between our engineering team, EPC partners, roofing contractors, and tenants on scheduling, access, and deliverables.
•       
Serve as the primary point of contact for routine project status inquiries from our institutional partner's team.
•       
Schedule and document project check-ins. Follow up on action items to ensure they're completed.
•       
Communicate with tenants on construction logistics, site access requirements, and timeline expectations.

Process Support

•        Support the interconnection application process by tracking submission deadlines, utility responses, and required documentation.
•       
Track permitting status across multiple jurisdictions and ensure EPC partners are meeting permitting timelines.
•       
Coordinate roof inspection scheduling with roofers and ensure re-roof work is completed ahead of solar installation.
•       
Assist with document management for construction-phase deliverables.

Qualifications

Required

•        1 to 3 years of experience in project coordination, project management, or a similar role. Solar, construction, or energy industry experience is a plus but not required.
•       
Exceptional organizational skills. You'll be tracking several projects simultaneously across multiple states and contractors.
•       
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. You'll be the go-between for internal teams, external partners, and clients.
•       
Proactive follow-up mindset. If something is due and hasn't been delivered, you follow up. If you haven't heard back, you follow up again. This is the core of the role.
•       
Proficiency with project tracking tools (Excel, Smartsheet, or similar).
•       
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
Preferred

•        Experience in solar, renewable energy, or commercial construction project management.
•       
Familiarity with utility interconnection processes and commercial building permitting.
•       
Experience working with institutional clients or large real estate portfolio owners.
•       
Comfort working in a small team environment where roles are flexible and ownership is expected.
What We Offer

•        A central role in one of the fastest-growing institutional solar programs in the country.
•       
Exposure to the full lifecycle of solar project development, from contract execution through energization.
•       
A small, collaborative team where your contributions are immediately visible and directly impact program success.
•       
Opportunity to grow into a project management role as the program scales.

jobs.description:
Overview

At UES, we’re a team of more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, geologists, inspectors, technicians, and drillers united by a shared purpose—to make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. As a national leader in geotechnical engineering, environmental consulting, and materials testing and inspection, we collaborate on transformative projects across transportation, energy, water, healthcare, and more. Learn more about the benefits of joining Team UES and our core values at careers.teamues.com.

Position Overview

We are seeking a motivated and hands-on Field Technician I to join our team and support engineering, environmental services, materials testing, and inspection projects. In this role, you will conduct on-site inspections, materials testing, and environmental sampling to ensure construction, infrastructure, and environmental projects meet industry standards and regulatory requirements.

As a Field Technician I, you will work alongside experienced professionals, gaining practical field experience, developing technical skills, and contributing to critical projects that impact communities. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, safety-conscious, and thrives in outdoor work environments, solving challenges in real time and collaborating with a team. This position requires frequent travel to job sites and offers excellent opportunities for growth, technical training, and career advancement in a dynamic industry.

To learn more about the important work our Field Technicians perform, here’s a short video: UES Field Technician

Responsibilities

Conduct field and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, asphalt, aggregate, and other construction materials to verify compliance with project specifications, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
Properly collect, label, and transport samples from job sites to laboratories for further testing and analysis.
Ensure that project testing requirements are met and compliant with project specifications, requirements, and company policies or procedures.
Complete detailed reports, logs, and documentation of test results, ensuring accuracy and timely submission to project managers and stakeholders.
Ensure all testing equipment is properly maintained, and functioning correctly, following company and manufacturer guidelines.
Accurately document test results, observations, and site conditions, preparing and submitting timely and detailed reports, logs, and presentations in accordance with company standards.
Communicate effectively with dispatch, field supervisors, contractors, and project managers, providing real-time updates on job status, site conditions, and any issues encountered.
Adhere to project timelines and schedules, reporting to job sites on time and completing assignments within established deadlines.
Adapt to changing project requirements, schedules, and weather conditions, maintaining flexibility to support business needs.
Participate in ongoing training and certification programs, as required, to maintain technical proficiency and industry compliance.
Follow strict safety protocols and OSHA regulations to maintain a safe work environment, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and adherence to company and client safety guidelines.
Operate and maintain an assigned company vehicle, including scheduling routine maintenance (oil changes, tire checks, fluid levels) and ensuring general cleanliness inside and out.
Perform other duties as assigned to support project goals and company initiatives.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; vocational training or coursework in construction, engineering, geology, or a related field is a plus.
0-3 years of experience in a field-based, outdoor, or physically demanding role preferred (construction, materials testing, geotechnical, or related industry experience is a plus).
Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record; ability to operate company-assigned vehicles safely.
Industry certifications as applicable such as ACI Level 1 Concrete Testing, or ability to obtain within a specified time period.
Commitment to workplace safety, following OSHA standards and company safety policies, including the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Basic computer proficiency, including experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Field Data Collection (FDC) software or similar industry tools.
Mathematical skills sufficient to add, subtract, multiply, and divide into all units of measure using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
Ability to read, write, and interpret blueprints, procedures, manuals, technical documents, and reports related to drilling, safety, and project requirements.
Efficient time management, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to complete tasks efficiently and accurately.
Attention to detail to ensure accurate sample collection, testing procedures, and documentation.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively, demonstrating a strong work ethic and commitment to producing high-quality results.
Flexibility to work varying schedules, including early mornings, weekends, overtime, and potential overnight travel as project demands require.

Travel Requirements

Relocation Notice:
UES is unable to provide or facilitate relocation for this position at this time. Candidates must currently reside within a reasonable commuting distance of the job location. Applicants who require relocation in order to accept this position will not be considered.

This position requires extensive travel, approximately up to 70% of the time, in support of business

objectives and client engagements. Travel may be both scheduled and on short notice, depending on

project needs. Destinations typically include job sites, field locations, or regional offices, where work may be conducted in outdoor or operational environments. Adherence to all company safety protocols and use of PPE is required during travel and on-site work.

Sites that may not be accessible by vehicle, requiring travel on foot through wetlands, swamps, grasslands, fields, and other uneven or rugged terrain with natural and man-made obstacles such as sand, brush, and debris.
Moderate to loud noise levels, common in active construction and industrial environments.
Exposure to environmental elements including dirt, dust, sun, heat, humidity, and adverse weather conditions.

The physical requirements for this position may include and are not limited to:

Ability to lift and/or carry 35 to 50 lbs. up to 75 feet, involving regular repetitive motion.
Ability to stand, walk, drive, and operate equipment for extended periods.
Frequent use of hands and arms for typing, handling tools, and operating equipment.
Ability to bend, twist, reach, stoop, pull, kneel, climb, balance, lift, carry, and push as required for fieldwork and inspections.
Ability to speak and hear effectively to communicate in noisy environments and with project teams.
Ability to use your senses to see (including close, distant, and peripheral vison, depth vision, and ability to focus) smell, hear, touch (use hands to reach climb or balance, crouch, stoop, crawl, kneel and sit).

Luminia is a San Diego–based clean energy developer founded in 2019 that partners with not-for-profit clean electricity providers across California to deliver distributed solar and energy storage projects. The company focuses on strengthening grid resilience and creating long-term community benefits through a hyper-local approach that combines technical and financial expertise with strong community engagement and respect for local values. Luminia specializes in urban and commercial project siting to streamline permitting and interconnection, helping keep energy rates competitive while advancing clean energy goals. For commercial and industrial property owners, Luminia offers flexible financing and turnkey development solutions that unlock the value of rooftops and land, lower energy costs, and support sustainability objectives. With over 100 MW of distributed solar and storage in development, Luminia is committed to equitable, scalable projects that benefit the grid, the economy, and the communities it serves.

The Role

We're looking for a Project Coordinator to serve as the organizational backbone of our institutional partnership project pipeline. You'll track active projects from PPA execution through system energization, coordinating across internal engineering, external EPC partners, roofing contractors, tenants, and our institutional partner's team.

This isn't a role where you'll be making engineering or financial decisions. It's a role where you'll be the person who knows exactly where every project stands, who's responsible for the next step, and whether it's on track. When something slips, you'll be the first to notice and the first to flag it. When the engineering team is heads-down on technical work or pulled to another program, you'll be the voice keeping the institutional partnership projects moving.

Think of this as the connective tissue between our engineering team, our EPC partners, and our clients. The job is to make sure information flows, deadlines are tracked, and nothing gets deprioritized without a conscious decision.

What You'll Do

Project Tracking and Status Management

•        Maintain a comprehensive project tracker covering active projects from PPA execution through construction completion and permission to operate (PTO).
•       
Track key milestones: interconnection application submission and approval, permitting status, roof inspection and re-roof coordination, equipment procurement, construction scheduling, and PTO.
•       
Provide regular status updates to internal leadership and flag slippage or risks before they become problems.
•       
Ensure institutional partnership projects maintain priority and visibility when team resources are shared across programs.

Coordination and Communication

•        Coordinate between our engineering team, EPC partners, roofing contractors, and tenants on scheduling, access, and deliverables.
•       
Serve as the primary point of contact for routine project status inquiries from our institutional partner's team.
•       
Schedule and document project check-ins. Follow up on action items to ensure they're completed.
•       
Communicate with tenants on construction logistics, site access requirements, and timeline expectations.

Process Support

•        Support the interconnection application process by tracking submission deadlines, utility responses, and required documentation.
•       
Track permitting status across multiple jurisdictions and ensure EPC partners are meeting permitting timelines.
•       
Coordinate roof inspection scheduling with roofers and ensure re-roof work is completed ahead of solar installation.
•       
Assist with document management for construction-phase deliverables.

Qualifications

Required

•        1 to 3 years of experience in project coordination, project management, or a similar role. Solar, construction, or energy industry experience is a plus but not required.
•       
Exceptional organizational skills. You'll be tracking several projects simultaneously across multiple states and contractors.
•       
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. You'll be the go-between for internal teams, external partners, and clients.
•       
Proactive follow-up mindset. If something is due and hasn't been delivered, you follow up. If you haven't heard back, you follow up again. This is the core of the role.
•       
Proficiency with project tracking tools (Excel, Smartsheet, or similar).
•       
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
Preferred

•       
Familiarity with utility interconnection processes and commercial building permitting.
•       
Experience working with institutional clients or large real estate portfolio owners.
•       
Comfort working in a small team environment where roles are flexible and ownership is expected.
What We Offer

•        A central role in one of the fastest-growing institutional solar programs in the country.
•       
Exposure to the full lifecycle of solar project development, from contract execution through energization.
•       
A small, collaborative team where your contributions are immediately visible and directly impact program success.

Job Summary

The Clerkship Coordinator provides comprehensive administrative and operational support for the Department of Anesthesiology and Perioperative Medicine's undergraduate medical education programs. This position coordinates all aspects of medical student clerkships, externships, visiting student rotations, observerships, and allied health student experiences, including scheduling, onboarding, evaluations, course management, and compliance activities.

Send calendar invitations to faculty/students for student lectures. Send student reminders for requirement due dates. Track completion of student requirements. Proctor ANES 5015 exam every 4 weeks. Liaison between Augusta and the Regional Campus Coordinators.

Complete Wellstar MCG Health Observership form. Obtain required signatures via DocuSign. Email completed packet to Mary Tipton for CMO approval. Once approved, liaise CMO's observer instructions to observer. Collect photo from observer and forward with badging form to Single Source to request observer ID badge. Assign locker, give observer orientation, ensure observer has clean scrubs each day, return used scrubs to be laundered.

*Job Summary and Responsibilities*

As our Mountain Rescue Program Coordinator, you will be a vital asset to Flight for Life (FFL), directly supporting program leadership and crew as a dedicated subject matter expert in backcountry helicopter search and rescue (SAR) operations. You will play a crucial role in enhancing the safety and effectiveness of our critical mountain rescue missions, contributing significantly to our life-saving services.

Every day, you will actively monitor backcountry SAR safety issues and emerging trends, developing and delivering essential safety education for helicopter SAR operations. You'll contribute your expertise to discussions aimed at improving safety protocols and training, not only within Flight for Life but also across Colorado. This role demands a proactive approach to identifying potential risks and implementing best practices to safeguard our teams and the public.

To be successful in this role, you will possess a deep understanding of backcountry helicopter SAR operations and a strong commitment to safety. Exceptional communication skills are key for collaborating with FFL leadership, crew, and external stakeholders. Ideal candidates will demonstrate a proactive mindset, an ability to analyze complex safety data, and a passion for continuous improvement in mountain rescue practices.

Serves the Flight for Life Program Director, leadership, and staff in development of all backcountry helicopter SAR Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Standard Operating Guidelines (SOGs).
Develops operational checklists and SAR member checkoff protocols of key FFL interagency SAR training programs.
Serves as Subject Matter Expert and develops SOPs/SOGs, checklists, and internal Operational Policies for SAR technology.
Makes recommendations pertaining to backcountry helicopter SAR operations to ensure safety of FFL crew and SAR rescuers.
Communicates protocols and procedures to the mountain rescue community, and represents Flight for Life on issues pertaining to backcountry helicopter SAR operations.
Serves on the Flight for Life Safety Committee, participating on matters pertaining to backcountry helicopter SAR operations, including review and assessment of specific SAR rescues as well as incident After Action Reviews as necessary.

*Job Requirements**Required*

High School Diploma/G.E.D.
Two (2) years Mountain Search and Rescue experience
Helicopter SAR Operations experience
Valid Colorado driver's license and ability to pass the annual review of driving record for safe vehicle operations
Search and Rescue Technician or HEMS Certificate

*Preferred*

Degree in Emergency Management, EMS, or equivalent
Prehospital experience
Air Medical and/or Rotorwing experience in alpine environments

Where You'll Work

Proudly part of CommonSpirit Health, Flight For Life Colorado® was the first civilian, hospital-based emergency medical helicopter program in the United States. For over 50 years, we have set the standard for over 300 air medical services worldwide that have modeled our concept. We proudly partner with search and rescue agencies, offering specialized services such as aerial search support and our Avalanche Deployment Program. Our reputation for rigorous training, comprehensive coverage, and proven expertise has made us the air medical program of choice for hospitals, EMS agencies, ski patrols, and rescue teams. With industry leading technology and a highly experienced team, we provide critical care transport across several states in the Rocky Mountain Region, including the Denver Metro area, Summit County, Colorado Springs, Pueblo, Durango, northern New Mexico, southeastern Utah, and western Kansas.
